To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the genomic structure, expression and functional characterization of STAT5 from fish were investigated.
the STAT5 gene is highly conserved at both genomic and protein levels and that the chimeric protein is a functional transcription factor.
the pufferfish STAT5 is similar to mammalian STATs at the levels of both genomic structure and biochemical properties.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the isolation, characterization of a STAT homologue from fish.
the identification of the STAT5 protein and its genomic organization in pufferfish.
the characterization of a STAT gene and protein from a non-mammalian species and provides the first insight into the function of STAT5 in fish.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the STAT5 protein of fish is a functional homologue of mammalian STAT5.
TfSTAT5 is a STAT5-like protein with a unique biochemical function.
TfSTAT5 is a functional homologue of STAT5a and 5b from mammalian species.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the fish STAT5 is a functional protein that can bind to and transactivate mammalian promoters, but it is not able to activate the beta-casein gene promoter via prolactin receptor in mammalian cells.
the fish STAT5 protein has a similar structure and function to the mammalian STAT5, but the fish STAT5 may have a unique role in the regulation of prolactin signaling.
fish STAT5 has the same biochemical properties as its mammalian counterpart.
The main takeaway from our work is that
fish STATs are functional in mammalian cells.
the STAT5 from pufferfish has the ability to bind to mammalian promoters, but not to activate them, suggesting that STAT5 from fish is not functional in the mammalian system.
the biochemical characteristics of TfSTAT5 are similar to those of mammalian STAT5, suggesting the conservation of STAT function in vertebrates.
